newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends up after late, scattered buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends up after late, scattered buying.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures erased earlier losses in the final hour of Wednesday trading on light scattered buying to end slightly higher.
Traders said some of the buying was short-covering by speculators who sold early looking for weakness after New York's mediocre close mid-range on Tuesday.
July closed up 13 stg at 1,026 stg per tonne and September rose 15 to 1,046. Volume reached 9,088 contracts, much of which was crossing, traders said.
March 1998 grabbed the most interest with 1,293 contracts changing hands. July and September were also active, trading about 642 and 560 lots, respectively.

Traders attributed the bulk of switch activity to large, French firm and a large, privately-held U.S. firm as the structure of the market tightened in the morning and then widened out again in the afternoon.

Cocoa lingered in negative ground for most of the day but when July failed to break through Tuesday's low, speculators turned around to test the upside. July broke Tuesday's high to edge up to the highest level since June 2. But volume remained unconvincing, and most traders still expected more range trading in the near-term.

Until fresh fundamental news or clearer technical signs emerged, traders expected July to remain trapped between the April 9 low of 980 and about 1,035. They said cocoa was just retesting the upper end of its range after 980 held last week to establish a triple bottom on daily charts.

If resistance holds, they expected another downside test soon, particularly before New York's first notice day on June 17. Speculative liquidation or rollover of July positions was expected to take London's July contract down to revisit 980.
In options, four July 1,000 calls, 25 September 975 puts and 25 September 1,150 calls traded.
